paragraphs: I've worked in Moraga long enough to know which homes on which streets tend to hold something special, and 206 Sheila Ct caught my attention right away. The combination of a mature fruit-tree side yard, that open family room layout with backyard access, and a floor plan that genuinely works for how people live today is not something you see on every block in this city. When I noticed the listing had come off the market without a sale, that's what prompted me to put this together for you.

At $885 per square foot, this home is priced at the very top of the Moraga range, and the features absolutely support that number. But a price at that level requires marketing that builds the case before buyers start comparing. Based on what I can see from the listing history, the strategy relied on a standard description and typical MLS distribution to carry a home that needed a stronger story. The fruit tree garden, the finished garage with sealed flooring, the dual outdoor spaces, the fourth bedroom on the main level. Those details add up to something meaningful for the right buyer. They just never got assembled into a narrative that landed.

I've put together a short analysis in this packet that walks through the specific friction points I see in how the listing was positioned, how the price sits relative to the Moraga market, and what a relaunch strategy would need to look like to connect with the buyers who would genuinely pay for what this home offers. It's not a pitch deck. It's the honest read I'd give anyone I was sitting across the table from.
If you're already working with an agent toward a new listing, please feel free to set this aside. If you're not, I'd welcome a short conversation whenever the timing feels right for you.

exec_summary.headline: A Refined Moraga Family Home With Genuine Depth  -  and a Listing That Didn't Show It
exec_summary.p1: 206 Sheila Ct has the combination Lamorinda buyers are actively looking for: a four-bedroom floor plan with a main-level guest room, a kitchen that opens directly to the family room and backyard, finished two-car garage with sealed floors and built-in storage, and an outdoor space that includes a grassy lawn, brick patio, and a producing fruit orchard. At 1,909 square feet on a 10,450-square-foot lot, the home delivers meaningful outdoor scale alongside a thoughtfully laid-out interior. These are real, marketable assets.
exec_summary.p2: The listing came off the market after just 21 days without a sale, which tells a specific story. At $1,690,000 and $885 per square foot, the home is priced at the ceiling of the Moraga premium tier. That ceiling is reachable, but only when the marketing builds a clear and specific case for why this home is worth the top of the range. A standard MLS description, however well-written, does not do that work on its own. The gap here was not the home's value. It was a strategy that put a premium price in front of buyers without giving them the visual and narrative evidence to feel confident about it.
exec_summary.p3: A relaunch for this property needs to do one thing above all else: close the gap between what buyers see on a screen and what they experience when they walk in. The backyard orchard, the dual living spaces, the finished garage, and the flexible fourth bedroom all need to be shown, not just mentioned. Buyers comparing homes at this price in Moraga need a reason to choose this one. The reason is already here.

forensics.title: Friction #1: Premium Not Justified in the Marketing
forensics.body: At $885 per square foot, 206 Sheila Ct is priced at the upper boundary of Moraga's premium tier, which runs $750 to $820 per square foot for well-appointed homes. That price is defensible given the lot size, the main-level fourth bedroom, the finished garage, and the producing fruit-tree side yard. But buyers comparing this home against others in the $1.6M to $1.7M Moraga range need to understand specifically what they're getting at that number that they won't find elsewhere. The listing described the features. It never built the case for the premium. Without that case, price-sensitive buyers moved on before they ever scheduled a showing.
forensics.brightwork_contrast: BrightWork's Zillow Showcase placement gives this home enhanced listing pages with expanded narrative space, premium visual positioning, and all buyer inquiries routed directly back to our team, so the story we build actually reaches the buyers researching at this price point.

forensics.title: Friction #2: The Visual Story Was Never Told
forensics.body: The outdoor spaces at this property are genuinely unusual for Moraga. A brick patio, a grassy lawn, a separate side yard planted with mature plum, orange, lemon, and apple trees, and backyard access directly from the family room through sliding doors. That is not a standard suburban backyard. It is a lifestyle asset that justifies a meaningful share of the asking price. Standard MLS photography rarely captures the sequence and scale of outdoor spaces like this in a way that translates online. Without the right visual, what should read as a rare outdoor setup registers as a generic backyard. Buyers scrolling at $1.6M-plus need to feel something before they commit to a showing, and flat photography of an interesting yard does not do that.
forensics.brightwork_contrast: A Sky Tour would show the lot position, the side yard scale, and the backyard setting from the air in a way no ground photo can replicate, giving buyers the spatial context to understand what they're actually looking at before they arrive.

forensics.title: Friction #3: The Right Buyers Were Never Actively Found
forensics.body: In mid-2026, the buyer pool for a $1,690,000 Moraga home is real but specific. These are typically dual-income households relocating from San Francisco or Oakland, often with children, who are researching Lamorinda schools and lifestyle online weeks or months before they contact an agent. A listing that enters the MLS and waits for those buyers to find it is competing on luck. Twenty-one days is not enough time for a passive strategy to reach the buyers who would pay $885 per square foot for the schools, the trails, and a floor plan like this one. The distribution never matched the price.
forensics.brightwork_contrast: BrightWork runs geo-targeted digital campaigns into San Francisco and East Bay zip codes where active Lamorinda researchers are concentrated, putting this home in front of the right buyers before they've found what they're looking for.

positioning_table.verdict: At $885/sqft versus a benchmark range of $750-$820/sqft, this home sits near the upper end of that range. At $885 per square foot, this home is priced above the top of Moraga's published premium tier. The lot size, the outdoor configuration, the kitchen build-out, and the flexible floor plan are all genuine assets that support a strong number. What the strategy needed to do was demonstrate that value specifically and visually to buyers making a careful comparison at this price point. The numbers are not the obstacle. The case that should have been built around them is where the gap sits.

pillars.title: Pillar I  -  Build the Premium Case Before the Listing Goes Live
pillars.body: At $885 per square foot, every detail of this home's story needs to be assembled and ready before a buyer sees the address on Zillow. The double ovens, the stone counters, the sealed garage floor, the main-level fourth bedroom. These are not incidental features. They are the reasons a buyer chooses this home over a comparable option priced lower. BrightWork builds the narrative and the visual package together, so the price makes sense the moment a buyer encounters the listing. That work happens before day one, not in response to days-on-market.

pillars.title: Pillar II  -  Show the Outdoor Spaces the Way They Deserve to Be Seen
pillars.body: The fruit-tree side yard and dual outdoor living areas at 206 Sheila Ct are a genuine differentiator, and they need media that communicates their scale and character. A 3D Matterport tour gives buyers the ability to walk through the full property from anywhere, including the flow from the family room through the sliding doors and into the backyard, at any hour, before they commit to a showing. Busy professionals and out-of-area buyers making decisions about a $1.6M-plus purchase need that kind of access. A static photo collection is not enough.

pillars.title: Pillar III  -  Reach the Buyers Who Are Already Looking for This Home
pillars.body: The households most likely to pay a premium for this specific combination of schools, trails, floor plan, and outdoor space are already researching Lamorinda from San Francisco and the East Bay. They may not have an agent yet, and they may not have found this address. BrightWork's off-market private buyer list at offmarket.brightworkrealty.com is a network of Bay Area buyers who have opted in to receive property alerts before anything hits public portals. A quiet preview to that audience could generate real interest before a public relaunch even begins.
